title: Scheduler-backed subnet fabric with IGW/NAT canary
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a Terraform module and operator workflow that creates an AZ-aware subnet fabric with scheduler-driven placement, IGW + NAT gateway provisioning, VPC endpoint reconciliation, and an automated canary rotation for NAT/egress paths. The module must support: 1) declarative subnet tiling (control plane determines subnet roles), 2) conditional NAT vs IGW egress per-subnet, 3) lifecycle hooks for safe upgrades (drain, detach, attach), and 4) active health probes that trigger automated rotation to standby NAT/IGW and failback policies. This ticket covers the module API, integration tests, upgrade hooks, and a canary rollout operator that swaps egress and validates connectivity via synthetic probes before full rollout.
acceptance_criteria:
- Terraform module exposes inputs for az_count, subnet_tiers, egress_policy, endpoint_whitelist, and upgrade_window
- Module provisions IGW and/or autoscaling NATs per-policy with tags for ownership and canary-stage
- Health probe Lambda (or equivalent) verifies DNS, egress IP, and S3/HTTP connectivity per-AZ and publishes metrics
- Canary operator can rotate one AZ at a time and automatically rollback on probe failure
- Integration test demonstrates zero-downtime control-plane updates for route table and endpoint changes
- Docs and example usage in private-deploying repo are merged
implementation_notes: Design decisions: prefer single Terraform module with two submodules (subnet-tiler, egress-controller) to keep state boundaries clear. Use resource-level lifecycle create_before_destroy where safe and introduce explicit drain_step outputs for external callers. For NATs prefer small fleet with warm-standby instances instead of large single NAT GW to reduce blast radius; use provider-managed autoscaling group on customer-approved template for Private deployments. Routing: route tables are explicit per-subnet-tier; endpoints (S3, Dynamo, KMS) are created via for_each maps and reconciled using a tag-based ownership strategy. Upgrade hooks: we will create 'pre_upgrade' and 'post_upgrade' null_resources that call the canary operator via AWS API/CLI. Trade-offs: more moving parts (operator + module) increases complexity but yields safer rollouts and faster recovery. Security: all egress NAT traffic will be tagged and logged; KMS encryption of state recommended in docs.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge module and unit tests behind feature flag in the private tf repo. 2) Deploy to staging VPC (single AZ) and run integration harness. 3) Enable canary operator to rotate egress in staging - validate probes. 4) Rollout to two non-critical customer VPCs (night window) with operator performing single-AZ canaries. 5) Monitor metrics for 48h, then full rollout. Emergency rollback: operator supports immediate revert to previous ENI/route mapping and reattach prior NATs.
monitoring_and_alerting:
- Health probe metric: subnet.egress.probe_success_rate (per-az, per-tier)
- Alert: probe_success_rate < 98% for 5min triggers P0 runbook to pause rollouts
- Cost/usage guard: new NAT autoscaling events > threshold triggers notify to infra-cost channel
- Dashboards: per-route latency, error rate for VPC endpoints, NAT instance CPU and connection counts
